strenda_biocatalysis_records.name: GalOx-ECR8215F
strenda_biocatalysis_records.description: Baseline biphasic oxidation of HMF to DFF using covalently immobilized galactose oxidase on Purolite Lifetech ECR8215F (epoxy carrier), in a 50:50 (v/v) 0.1 M NaPi buffer (pH 7.4) / ethyl acetate biphasic system. Reaction conditions and DFF yield reproduced in Figure S1 and as batch 1 of Figure 3.

identity.name: Galactose oxidase (GalOx)
identity.ec_number_note: Not stated in the publication. For reference only (NOT from this paper): galactose oxidase is classified as EC 1.1.3.9 per the ExPASy/IUBMB enzyme nomenclature database, https://enzyme.expasy.org/EC/1.1.3.9.
identity.catalyzed_reaction: Oxygen-dependent oxidation of primary alcohols (e.g. D-galactose, 5-hydroxymethylfurfural/HMF) to the corresponding aldehydes (e.g. D-galacto-hexodialdose, 2,5-diformylfuran/DFF), with concomitant reduction of O2 to H2O2 (paper Introduction and Figure S3).
identity.origin_organism_note: Not stated in the publication (source organism of the commercial GalOx preparation is not given).

source.supplier_note: Not explicitly stated for GalOx itself in the Materials section. The Lifetech(TM) enzyme carriers were supplied by Purolite Ltd. (United Kingdom); GalOx is described only as 'a commercial preparation' without naming the vendor.

purchased_details.formulation_note: Used/handled as a liquid enzyme solution (2 mg/mL) during immobilization; exact commercial formulation not stated.

application.application_type_note: Enum approximation — paper states 'commercial preparation of galactose oxidase', purity not specified; closest available enum value chosen, not a verified claim of purified enzyme.

immobilization.biocatalyst_state: Commercial enzyme preparation, liquid solution (2 mg/mL) at the point of immobilization.
immobilization.immobilisation_chemistry: Covalent, multipoint attachment: surface amino groups of GalOx perform a nucleophilic ring-opening attack on the carrier's epoxy groups, forming a covalent bond; no activation step or crosslinker required for epoxy carriers (main text, 'Carrier screening for immobilization').
immobilization.carrier_material: Purolite® Lifetech(TM) ECR8215F — epoxy-functionalized methacrylate macroporous resin, particle size 150-300 µm, pore diameter 1200-1800 Å.
immobilization.linkers: None (epoxy carriers require no crosslinker/activation, unlike amino carriers which need glutaraldehyde).
immobilization.immobilisation_method: Carrier washed in 0.1 M NaPi buffer pH 7.4 (1:1 w:v) for 5 min, liquid removed by vacuum filtration. Washed carrier mixed with 2 mg/mL GalOx solution for 18 h at room temperature and 60 rpm. Mixture vacuum filtered and washed twice. Immobilized enzyme stored at 4°C (Experimental Section, 'Enzyme immobilization procedure'; manufacturer protocol ref. [48]).
immobilization.purification_method: Vacuum filtration and two washing steps after immobilization.

loading.determination_method: Protein loading = (offered enzyme (mg) - total enzyme in supernatants (mg)) / wet carrier (g); measured via Bradford assay (Table 1; error ±0.5).

immobilization.notes: ECR8215F (epoxy) was selected for all downstream oxidation experiments as the optimal carrier: highest activity yield (28.3 ± 0.6%) among epoxy carriers plus high absolute activity retained after 4 weeks of storage (47.5 ± 4.9% of initial activity), even though ECR8285 (butyl/epoxy) showed better *relative* storage stability (65.2 ± 12.9% after 4 weeks).

storage.notes: Immobilized enzyme stored at 4°C after washing (Experimental Section, 'Enzyme immobilization procedure').

provenance.supplier: Sigma-Aldrich (Germany) [inferred: 'all other chemicals' not individually listed were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich and used as received] — not individually named for HMF in the Materials list.

reaction_components.notes: Non-natural substrate for wild-type GalOx (Conclusions). Adsorbs to ECR8215F carrier: ~15% bound in NaPi buffer after 72 h; negligible adsorption in EtOAc (Figure 2).

provenance.supplier: Not individually specified; general chemicals from Sigma-Aldrich (Germany).

amount.note: Variable v/v fraction depending on experiment (see reaction_conditions).

provenance.supplier: Not individually specified; general chemicals from Sigma-Aldrich (Germany).

feeding.description: Single substrate charge at t=0; no feeding during the reaction.

operation_mode.notes: All oxidation reactions were run as closed-vial batch reactions (Experimental Section).

multiphasic.notes: Aqueous NaPi buffer phase (pH 7.4) + ethyl acetate organic phase, 50:50 v/v.

phases.material_description: 0.1 M NaPi buffer, pH 7.4 (aqueous phase); immobilized biocatalyst partitions here.

detection.detected_when: Not specified (buffer prepared at pH 7.4; not stated whether monitored during reaction).

pH.notes: pH of the aqueous (NaPi buffer) phase only; pH of the biphasic/organic system as a whole not reported.

reaction_conditions.notes: 50 mM HMF; 3 mL total liquid volume in 30 mL reaction vials; 25°C; 170 rpm; 72 h reaction time (main text, 'Oxidation of HMF to DFF...' and Table 2 legend).

kinetics.enzyme_stability: Immobilized biocatalyst loses activity with reuse: in 50% v/v H2O-EtOAc, yield in batch 2 was <=50% of batch 1; over 5 consecutive 72 h batches (4 recycles) total product-formation loss was 80% (Figure 3).

yield_and_conversion.notes: DFF yield 2.9 ± 0.4% after 72 h (main text and Table 2 baseline comparison; consistent with the 50% v/v H2O point at t=72h in Figure S1).

results.notes: Reaction plateaued around 48 h in most water-content conditions tested (Figure S1). Authors note actual DFF formed may be ~1.67x higher than the reported/measured yield once adsorptive loss of DFF onto the carrier (~40% in aqueous phase) is accounted for.

table_1_carrier_screening.description: Immobilization parameters for GalOx on 10 Purolite Lifetech carriers (amino- and epoxy-functionalized).
table_1_carrier_screening.notes: ECR8404F/8409F/8415F (long-spacer amino carriers) showed no measurable activity despite relatively high immobilization yields (main text). Immobilization yield (%) = (offered enzyme (g) - total enzyme in supernatants (g)) / offered enzyme (g). Activity yield (%) = [Activity_immobilized (U/g_wet_carrier) x mass_wet_carrier (g)] / [Activity_free_enzyme (U/mg_enzyme) x offered_enzyme (g)] (formulas in Table 1 footnote).

table_2_semipreparative_scale.description: Oxidation of 50 mM HMF to DFF in 50% v/v H2O-EtOAc using GalOx-ECR8215F at 25°C, 170 rpm, 72 h, with a fixed 9:1 headspace:liquid volume ratio. Biological triplicates, HPLC analysis.

figure_1_storage_stability.description: Relative residual activity (%) of GalOx immobilized on 4 epoxy-functionalized carriers over 28 days storage at 4°C, relative to day-1 activity. Reaction conditions: 1 mM ABTS, 100 mM D-galactose, 2 U/mL HRP, 0.1 M NaPi buffer pH 7.4, 10 mL reaction volume, 5 mg immobilized enzyme, 25°C. Biological duplicates.

carriers.ECR8204F: Values read from graph only (no exact numbers given in text besides day-28 comparisons); day-1 normalized to 100%.
carriers.ECR8209F: 47.3 ± 6.4% activity retained after 4 weeks (day 28), per main text.
carriers.ECR8215F: 47.5 ± 4.9% activity retained after 4 weeks (day 28), per main text.
carriers.ECR8285: 65.2 ± 12.9% activity retained after 4 weeks (day 28) — best RELATIVE stability of the 4 carriers tested, per main text.

figure_1_storage_stability.notes: Only the day-28 percentages for ECR8209F, ECR8215F and ECR8285 are given as exact numbers in the main text; all other time points are visual/graphical only (Figure 1) and were NOT digitized/estimated here to avoid inventing precision not present in the source.

figure_2_adsorption.description: Adsorption of HMF and DFF onto Purolite Lifetech ECR8215F (epoxy) carrier in 0.1 M NaPi buffer pH 7.4 and in neat ethyl acetate. Reaction conditions: 0.250 g ECR8215F, 50 mM HMF or DFF, 3 mL total liquid volume in 30 mL vials, 25°C, 170 rpm, 72 h. Biological triplicates; residual HMF/DFF quantified by HPLC.
findings: EtOAc: negligible adsorption detected for both HMF and DFF (qualitative; exact % not given in text).
Buffer: ~15% of HMF adsorbed to the carrier after 72 h.
Buffer: ~40% of DFF adsorbed to the carrier within the first 24 h (near-plateau thereafter, likely due to reaching a critical/saturating concentration on the carrier).
figure_2_adsorption.notes: Exact time-resolved percentage values are shown only graphically in Figure 2; only the summary percentages stated explicitly in the main text are reproduced above.

figure_S1_water_content_screening.description: DFF yield (%) vs. time for GalOx-ECR8215F catalyzed HMF oxidation across a range of EtOAc:0.1 M NaPi-buffer(pH 7.4) biphasic compositions. Conditions: 0.250 g GalOx-ECR8215F, 50 mM HMF, 3 mL total liquid volume in 30 mL vials, 25°C, 170 rpm. Biocatalyst replaced with a fresh batch at 72 h and the reaction continued for a further 72 h (total 144 h). Biological triplicates.
figure_S1_water_content_screening.notes: Individual numeric yield values at each time point/condition are presented only graphically in Figure S1 and were not digitized here (to avoid fabricating precision absent from the source). Text-stated summary values: highest overall yield achieved at 50:50 v/v EtOAc:buffer, reaching 2.9 ± 0.4% after the first 72 h and 9.0 ± 0.8% after the second 72 h with a fresh catalyst batch (matches the ~9% cluster visible for the 50% v/v H2O series at 120-144 h in the figure). Reaction reached a plateau around 48 h in most conditions.

figure_3_batch_recycling.description: Yield of DFF (%) over 5 consecutive 72 h reaction cycles using the SAME immobilized GalOx-ECR8215F batch (washed and reintroduced to fresh substrate after each cycle), compared across 3 media. Conditions: 0.250 g GalOx-ECR8215F, 50 mM HMF, 3 mL total liquid volume in 30 mL vials, 25°C, 150 rpm. Biological triplicates, HPLC analysis.
summary_findings: In all three media, the yield in batch 2 was <=50% of the yield in batch 1.
Cumulative product-formation loss after 5 batches (4 recycles), relative to batch 1: 44% loss in neat EtOAc, 80% loss in 50% v/v H2O-EtOAc, 89% loss in buffer.
Smaller batch-to-batch (2->5) differences were observed as the EtOAc fraction of the medium increased.
figure_3_batch_recycling.notes: Individual per-batch yield values for each medium are shown only graphically (Figure 3) and are not stated as exact numbers in the text; only the qualitative/aggregate statements above are given explicitly in the source and were extracted.

figure_S2_agglomerates.source: Figure S2 (Supporting Information) and main text
figure_S2_agglomerates.description: Photograph showing formation of spherical agglomerates of GalOx-ECR8215F in water-saturated/neat EtOAc. Conditions: 0.250 g GalOx-ECR8215F, 50 mM HMF, 3 mL total liquid volume in 30 mL vials, 25°C, 72 h, 170 rpm.
figure_S2_agglomerates.interpretation: Immobilized enzyme particles cluster around scarce water molecules under low-water conditions, occluding enzyme immobilized at the centre of the agglomerate from substrate access and lowering apparent yields (main text).

analytical_methods.hplc: HPLC analysis: Agilent Technologies 1260 Infinity II HPLC with diode-array detector (DAD); Rezex(TM) ROA Organic Acid H+ column (8%), 300x7.8 mm (Phenomenex); isocratic elution with 0.005 N H2SO4 in Milli-Q water, flow rate 0.75 mL/min, column temperature 50°C, total runtime 42 min; injection volume 10 µL; HMF and DFF detected at 280.4 nm (Experimental Section, 'HPLC analysis'; ref. [51]).
analytical_methods.abts_hrp_activity_assay: Activity measured with a modified ABTS-HRP coupled spectrophotometric assay (ref. [49]): 1 mM ABTS, 100 mM D-galactose, 2 U/mL horseradish peroxidase (HRP) in 100 mM NaPi buffer pH 7.4; H2O2 generated by GalOx oxidation of D-galactose is used by HRP to oxidize ABTS to its coloured cation radical, monitored at 405 nm and 25°C (molar extinction coefficient epsilon = 30.9 L min mmol^-1). Free-enzyme/supernatant activity: 10 µL sample + 990 µL assay mix, continuous monitoring for 1 min. Immobilized-enzyme activity: 5 mg catalyst in 10 mL assay solution under stirring, single-point absorbance on five 1 mL samples taken at 20 s intervals. All activity measurements in triplicate. 1 U = amount of enzyme consuming 1 µmol O2/min, or oxidizing 2 µmol ABTS/min.
analytical_methods.bradford_protein_assay: Protein quantification via Bradford assay (ref. [50]), microplate-adapted for low protein concentrations (1-25 µg/mL): 150 µL sample + 150 µL Bradford reagent per well, shaken 30 s, incubated 10 min, absorbance read at 595 nm (Tecan Infinite M200 PRO plate reader). Standard curve constructed with Albumin bovine fraction V (Serva), pH 7.0.

well_covered_by_paper: Biocatalyst.immobilization (chemistry, carrier material, method, loading) — extensively detailed for all 10 carriers.
ReactionConditions.temperature (constant 25°C), reaction system (biphasic, 2 phases), operation mode (batch).
Results.yield_and_conversion.product_yield — reported with SD for most conditions (Table 2, main text, Figure 3/4 aggregate values).
VesselAndMixing — vessel volumes, headspace:liquid ratio, shaking speed (170/150 rpm) given.
Sampling — HPLC method fully described (column, eluent, flow, detection wavelength).
gaps_or_under_specification_in_paper: BiocatalystIdentity.ec_number, molecular_weight, origin_organism, production_organism, sequences — none reported (commercial GalOx not further characterized).
BiocatalystSource.supplier — not explicitly named for the GalOx enzyme itself (only carrier supplier, Purolite, is named).
PurchasedDetails.purity / purity_specification — not reported for GalOx.
KineticResults (Km, Vmax, kcat, kcat/Km, Ki) — no Michaelis-Menten or inhibition kinetics reported; only yields and specific activities.
SelectivityResults and ThermodynamicResults — entirely unaddressed (reaction is not stereoselective; no ΔG/ΔH/ΔS data).
PHDetection (how/when pH was measured) and ReactionConditions.pH profile beyond the fixed buffer pH — not described.
Sample-level metadata (exact sample volume, quenching method) — not explicitly stated; inferred as 'not specified'.
ComponentIdentity.smiles/identifiers (CAS, PubChem, InChI) — not given for any reagent in the paper (chemical names/structures only).
optional_fields_paper_could_add: SMILES/CAS numbers for HMF, DFF, D-galactose, ABTS to improve machine interoperability.
Explicit GalOx supplier/catalog number and stated purity.
Exact sample aliquot volume for HPLC injections beyond the 10 µL injection volume already reported.
model_extension_ideas_not_yet_proposed: ComponentRole enum has no 'product' value (only substrate/cosubstrate/buffer/salt/solvent/ion/cofactor/coenzyme/other) — DFF had to be tagged 'other'.
No structured field for time-resolved adsorption/partitioning of a component onto a solid support (relevant for Figure 2 data) — captured only as free-text notes here.
No structured field for biocatalyst recycling/reuse across sequential batches (batch number, yield per batch) — relevant for Figure 3/Table 1 storage-stability-style data; captured only as free text.
OperationMode / FeedingStrategy models feeding of REAGENTS, not periodic REPLACEMENT of the solid catalyst itself (Figure 4) — had to be shoehorned into 'fed_batch' + notes.
